newsitem.title: INDIA: India approves $560 mln foreign investments.
newsitem.headline: India approves $560 mln foreign investments.

text.p: The Indian government announced approval on Thursday for foreign investments worth $560 million in 142 separate projects.
An official statement said Industry Minister Murasoli Maran approved the investments with a projected export value of $1.65 billion.
Maran cleared a $39 million investment in software and cable television technology by the U.S.-based Falcon International.
Another $39 million investment was cleared for the retail sector by the Dutch firm SHV Makro NV, the statement said.
South Korea's LG Electronics Inc was cleared to invest $57 million in the consumer durables sector.
The announcement did not provide details of the individual projects.
With Thursday's approvals, the number of projects cleared for foreign investments has gone up to 950 involving 190 billion rupees since July 1996, the statement said.
Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's government took office on June 1 last year.
Foreign investments cleared since India launched its economic reforms in 1991 include more than 5,640 projects worth 960 billion rupees, the statement said.
Thursday's announcement came a day before Deve Gowda was due to leave for Davos, Switzerland, where he is expected to clear recent doubts over his government's commitment to reforms.
